Future Expansion Plans

BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia has indicated that the governing body intends to initiate formal discussions regarding the potential expansion of the Women's Premier League (WPL). While no concrete changes have been finalized, the board plans to review the current structure and explore the feasibility of increasing the number of participating teams in the coming year.

Current Status of the League

Since its inception in 2023, the WPL has operated with a format featuring five teams. The league serves as a primary fixture in the professional franchise cricket landscape, following the model established by the Indian Premier League (IPL).

Key points regarding the league's development include:

  • Establishment: The tournament launched in 2023 with five foundational teams.
  • Growth Impact: According to the BCCI secretary, the league has contributed significantly to the development and strengthening of women's cricket in India over the past few years.
  • Strategic Review: The BCCI is currently assessing the progress of the league to determine how to better foster growth for the sport moving forward.

Verification and Next Steps

As of now, the league remains in a evaluation phase. Interested stakeholders and cricket enthusiasts can monitor the official BCCI portal or press releases for future announcements regarding changes to team rosters or tournament formats. Any updates regarding expansion or logistical shifts for future seasons will be provided through formal BCCI channels.
